mustKnow.title: Trump set to lurch further right, claiming US took ‘giant step back’ in elections
mustKnow.snippet: Trump plans tougher immigration enforcement and will resist Democratic House demands after the midterm losses, with Stephen Miller becoming chief of staff.
mustKnow.brief: Trump said the US took a "giant step back" after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in last week's midterms, and his administration appears set to press ahead with its agenda. Stephen Miller will become White House chief of staff on Monday, and Trump has offered Dana White the press secretary job. Democrats plan investigations into Elon Musk and Miller once they take control of the House in January.
mustKnow.why: Stephen Miller as chief of staff signals no post-midterm moderation

mustKnow.title: Israel’s president picks Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to form government
mustKnow.snippet: Herzog has tasked Yashar leader Eisenkot with forming a government after a deadlocked election that cost Netanyahu his majority.
mustKnow.brief: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, with forming a new government after an October election left neither him nor Benjamin Netanyahu with a clear path to power. Eisenkot's bloc won 48 of 120 seats while Netanyahu's camp took 53, so Eisenkot needs 61 votes and has 28 days to assemble them, with a possible 14-day extension. Arab-majority lists, who could act as kingmakers, have endorsed him, but his conditions and divisions among partners make a deal uncertain.
mustKnow.why: Eisenkot has six weeks; success would end Netanyahu era

mustKnow.title: Islamist Militant Attack Forces Patients to Flee Ebola Clinic in Congo
mustKnow.snippet: At least 48 killed in an Islamic State-linked assault, forcing patients to flee an Ebola treatment clinic during a growing outbreak.
mustKnow.brief: An attack by militants loyal to the Islamic State killed at least 48 people in Congo, according to officials. The assault took place in an area that is a hot spot of the expanding Ebola outbreak, which is why it has drawn attention to the country's health response. The source does not say how the violence affected patients or treatment centers, so those details remain unclear.
mustKnow.why: Violence disrupting Ebola care risks wider, uncontrolled spread

mustKnow.title: Saudi Aramco Tower Damaged as Yemen’s Houthis Attack Riyadh
mustKnow.snippet: Falling shrapnel from Houthi missiles hit the Aramco tower in Riyadh's financial district, with no casualties reported.
mustKnow.brief: Saudi authorities said no one was injured after falling debris from an intercepted attack struck a building in Riyadh's financial district, an area among the most prominent targets of the Houthi rebels in Yemen. The brief feed summary does not name the tower, confirm the extent of damage, or give details of the attack itself, so further specifics remain unclear.
mustKnow.why: Houthi strike on Riyadh widens Gulf war; oil markets watch

mustKnow.title: Cop31 must deliver climate progress that people can see is real, host says
mustKnow.snippet: Cop31 talks in Turkey with nearly 190 countries begin Monday amid the strongest El Niño on record, which is expected to cause major losses.
mustKnow.brief: Scores of world leaders and delegates from close to 190 countries are gathering in Turkey for UN climate talks that open Monday, with the Cop31 host insisting the summit deliver a visible, real outcome. Talks come as the strongest El Niño on record, supercharged by fossil fuels, is expected to cost hundreds of thousands of lives and trillions of dollars. Friction is likely over who pays for climate damage, with the US sending no delegation for a second year.
mustKnow.why: Record El Niño backdrop; watch finance and emissions pledges

cleantech.title: US datacenter demand spurs increased fossil fuel pipeline projects as rules are discarded
cleantech.snippet: A federal records review found nearly 200 proposed or ongoing pipeline projects tied to data-centre demand and gas exports.
cleantech.brief: A Environmental Integrity Project review of federal records found nearly 200 proposed or under-way pipeline projects spanning about 17,000 miles, driven partly by datacenter power needs and gas exports. Critics warn the Trump administration is loosening safety and environmental rules, including pledging not to enforce pipeline regulations, while the US already logs about 1.7 pipeline accidents daily. Advocates say the buildout could strain communities and wetlands, with at least 81 projects expected to damage over 19,000 acres of protected wetlands.
cleantech.why: Data-centre load is locking in ~200 new gas pipelines

cleantech.title: A New $1.5 Billion Wind Farm Will Play In Peoria
cleantech.snippet: Repsol plans a 500 MW, $1.5 billion wind farm in Illinois despite federal policy reversals on energy.
cleantech.brief: Peoria County's board approved Repsol's Four Creeks wind project on a 12-5 vote, attaching 36 conditions mostly covering construction and operations. The company plans roughly 113 turbines on about 27,000 acres of private land, with each turbine occupying under an acre. Repsol still needs construction permits, and the timeline could stretch to about five years before building starts.
cleantech.why: 500 MW at $3M/MW shows wind still pencils post-IRA rollback

cleantech.title: Even California’s Biggest Ports Aren’t Betting On Hydrogen For Ships
cleantech.snippet: Long Beach and Los Angeles ports are not planning hydrogen for ships despite California's long support of the fuel.
cleantech.brief: The ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach released a Clean Marine Fuel Feasibility Assessment in October that left hydrogen out of detailed deep-sea fuel planning. They recommend methanol bunkering demonstrations and continued LNG arrangements while avoiding major new terminals. Of 38 shipping lines contacted, 19 responded, and only one expressed interest in hydrogen, compared with nine for methanol.
cleantech.why: Hydrogen's maritime case weakens even in its strongest US market

cleantech.title: Labour expected to cut EV targets for UK’s car industry despite MPs’ protests
cleantech.snippet: Steep cuts to UK EV sales mandates are expected, weakening a key part of the emissions reduction plan.
cleantech.brief: Ministers are expected to cut the UK's electric vehicle sales target by about a quarter, with Louise Haigh reportedly set to settle a 2030 mandate near 60% and extend flexibilities to 2034. The move would ease pressure on carmakers, who say the interim targets are out of reach, with battery EVs at 26.6% of sales in the first ten months of the year against a 33% goal. Labour MPs and the EV charging industry, which cites £1.7bn of infrastructure at risk, warn the decision weakens the government's main decarbonisation policy.
cleantech.why: Softer ZEV mandates dent European EV and battery demand

cleantech.title: Petrobras analyzes oil areas in Mexico to detect development opportunities
cleantech.originalTitle: Petrobras analiza áreas petroleras en México para detectar oportunidades de desarrollo
cleantech.snippet: Petrobras is running seismic surveys across eight Gulf of Mexico areas and mature fields to find new exploration prospects.
cleantech.brief: Pemex's third-quarter financial report says Brazil's Petrobras has begun evaluating Mexican oil areas under a memorandum of understanding signed in June 2026. Since September 1, Petrobras has received geological, geophysical and well data from the Energy Secretariat, and seismic studies are underway in eight areas within the Gulf of Mexico. The work aims to identify and prioritize exploration opportunities, including mature fields and presalt reservoirs, which matter because Pemex faces operational challenges in deepwater exploration.
cleantech.why: Foreign upstream interest tests Mexico's Pemex-centric energy model

ai.title: Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" exposes passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files
ai.snippet: Researchers found that a permission setting in Claude Code led to credentials being committed to 1,122 public GitHub repositories.
ai.why: Agent permission defaults leaking secrets; check your own repos

ai.title: After the midterms, things are looking rocky for Elon Musk and data centers
ai.snippet: Analysis suggests post-election policy shifts could create headwinds for Musk's businesses and data-centre buildouts.
ai.brief: After this week's midterm elections, voters in dozens of local ballot measures rejected data centers, and newly elected officials such as Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on restricting them. Hosts on TechCrunch's Equity podcast argued that Elon Musk's roughly half-billion-dollar Republican donations bought him little, since his companies are now based in a state that turned sharply blue. OpenAI has responded by dropping NDA requirements for its compute campus projects, a sign that regulatory pressure could push companies to change how they build.
ai.why: New Democratic House could slow data-centre power and permitting

ai.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
ai.snippet: The new suit adds Tennessee right-of-publicity claims to ongoing copyright fights, targeting Suno's generation of music mimicking the two artists.
ai.brief: Two new lawsuits have been filed against Suno, the AI music company, by Elvis Presley rights holders and the publisher of Eminem's major hits. Both accuse Suno of producing songs and lyrics that imitate these artists without permission. The Presley case invokes Tennessee's ELVIS Act, which bans AI cloning of a singer's voice, and the filings follow a similar September suit brought by Jason Isbell and others.
ai.why: Publicity-rights claims add a new legal front against generative models

ai.title: Llama-modchip: 284B DeepSeek on 64GB RAM, no GPU
ai.snippet: A hobbyist project runs a very large DeepSeek model on a consumer machine with 64GB RAM and no GPU.
ai.brief: A GitHub project called llama-modchip claims it can run DeepSeek-V4-Flash, a 284-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, entirely in system RAM on a CPU workstation with 64 to 128 GB of DDR5 and no GPU. The project says this avoids disk swapping and removes the need for multi-GPU hardware costing over $30,000. The text is largely promotional and offers no independent benchmark results, and its custom tensor format means standard llama.cpp, Ollama, or LM Studio builds will not load the models without patches.
ai.why: CPU-only inference of huge MoE models lowers hardware bar

world.title: The INE faces its breakdown 36 years after giving way to democracy in Mexico
world.originalTitle: El INE se enfrenta a su descomposición 36 años después de haber dado paso a la democracia en México
world.snippet: The electoral institute faces a severe crisis after a corruption scandal involving its former president Guadalupe Taddei.
world.brief: Mexico's electoral institute, the INE, is in its worst crisis after a corruption scandal involving its president, Guadalupe Taddei, who is accused of colluding with suppliers of electoral material. Experts say the roots go back decades, to a system built on mutual distrust and a costly design that left it vulnerable. The institute faces a budget cut of 5,000 million pesos and must rebuild credibility before the midterm elections.
world.why: Electoral authority's collapse threatens Mexico's democratic checks

world.title: For Trump and America, a Clear Election Verdict but a Murky Future
world.snippet: The US election result is clear, but the timing of Trump's departure from the presidency leaves uncertainty about the next months.
world.why: Uncertainty over Trump's exit timing reshapes coming months

world.title: Healthcare, tariffs – but not Trump impeachment: Democrats chart next two years of power
world.snippet: Democrats now have new leverage over Trump after winning the House, with healthcare and tariffs likely priorities.
world.brief: Democrats won control of Congress in the midterms, giving them new leverage over President Trump, and their incoming leaders plan aggressive investigations and legislation aimed at the 2028 race. Jeffries named restoring ACA premium tax credits, undoing Medicaid cuts, and reversing tariffs as priorities, but impeachment is not on the table. Trump remains in office until January 2029 and can veto bills, and the Senate filibuster still stands, so Republicans can block many Democratic bills.
world.why: Tariff oversight priority matters for US–Mexico trade

world.title: US task force to cut off Iran’s transport of advanced weapons: What we know
world.snippet: Washington has launched a task force aimed at interdicting Iranian shipments of advanced weapons amid rising escalation fears.
world.why: Naval interdiction raises risk of direct US–Iran clashes

world.title: Texas Led on Hard-Line Immigration Policies. Democrats Plan a Reversal.
world.snippet: A Democratic sweep in Texas could shift state immigration enforcement and push back against aggressive ICE tactics.
world.brief: Democrats are planning to reverse Texas's hard-line immigration approach, according to a New York Times summary. The source points to a Democratic sweep in the state as a sign of fresh momentum toward curbing aggressive ICE tactics. The summary gives no specific policy details, vote counts, or timeline, so the broader plans remain unclear from this brief excerpt alone.
world.why: Texas reversal could change border enforcement affecting Mexico
